product.name: MVA Transparent Prioritizer
product.mission: Produce an auditable local research ranking from controlled MVA phenotype and VCF inputs while keeping every patient-level value inside the encrypted workspace.
product.core_output: A private candidate dossier plus a separate public-safe methods and learnings packet.
product.hero_workflow: Verify receipts, run synthetic acceptance, execute the offline private pipeline, review a reasoned candidate dossier, then build a privacy-scanned public projection.
product.differentiation: It wraps established rare-disease tools with strict path confinement, exact provenance, independent evidence lanes, tamper detection, and a tested public-private projection boundary.
non_goals: Diagnosis, treatment, dose, safety, or clinical benefit claims
Automatic challenge submission, publication, repository push, or messaging
Hosted processing of protected case data
Use or reconstruction of a hidden confirmed answer
FASTQ processing without a named analytical gap

problem.target_user: Jonathan, acting as the local research operator for the MVA Hackathon case
problem.painful_job: Turn a controlled phenotype document and whole-genome VCF into a short, reproducible candidate list that a specialist can audit under time pressure.
problem.current_workaround: Run annotation and phenotype tools separately, compare spreadsheets manually, and assemble a report without one deterministic receipt or enforced public-private boundary.
evidence: Official Track 1 requires ranked candidate rows and a methods report: https://huggingface.co/spaces/SageBio/rare-disease-real-kid-mva-hackathon-2026/blob/main/tabs/submit_track1.py
The controlled dataset supplies a phenotype document and GRCh38 VCF: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SageBio/mva-hackathon-2026-data/blob/main/README.md
Content-free local inspection on 2026-08-26 confirmed one sample, GRCh38 plus decoys, genotype quality fields, and explicit HPO identifiers
problem.frequency: At least one full analysis cycle, plus replay after each reference, configuration, code, or evidence change before submission.
problem.consequence: A weak or opaque ranking can waste review time, miss a plausible mechanism, expose protected data, or create false clinical confidence.
problem.value_hypothesis: A confined, receipt-bound workflow will make candidate review faster and make every ranking reason challengeable without weakening privacy.
problem.success_metric: One deterministic synthetic replay and one private review-ready run whose candidate rows all carry provenance, quality, phenotype, inheritance, and uncertainty fields.
problem.kill_criteria: Stop on unresolved reference identity, any protected export, failed path containment, or stale evidence. Move to a named analytical-gap decision when coding and targeted non-coding lanes yield no credible candidate.

alternatives: Direct Exomiser execution with manual review
bcftools and VEP with spreadsheet curation
Hosted-model variant review, excluded for protected case data
workflow_observations: Track 1 accepts one-variant and paired-variant rows and sorts by submitted confidence.
The supplied VCF has one sample and no advertised consequence annotation.
The phenotype document contains explicit HPO identifiers, so local deterministic extraction is feasible.
The VCF header does not advertise structural-variant fields, so variant-class coverage needs an explicit warning.
research.market_gap: Established tools rank variants, but the case needs a small offline layer that enforces privacy, proves provenance, preserves independent evidence lanes, and creates a safe public projection.
constraints: Protected runtime has 8 GB memory and Apple Silicon.
Private execution must be offline and remain inside the encrypted workspace.
Single-sample data limits inheritance and phase conclusions.
Public output cannot contain patient-level values or row-level derivatives.
Controlled and derived data follow the challenge deletion deadline.
Scientific review remains required before any clinical use.

criteria: Unsafe paths and tampered receipts fail before private content is read or written.
Private execution emits content-free status and detailed files only under the private root.
Every candidate preserves source score, evidence reasons, inheritance uncertainty, and provenance.
No-result and unsupported-variant-class states remain explicit.
The public projection passes seeded-canary and forbidden-field scans.
Independent review covers exact current commit and all valid blockers are resolved.

experience.direction: A staged, receipt-first operator CLI with content-free stdout and detailed private files.

color: Optional ANSI disabled when output is redirected

architecture.system_context: Public code and reference acquisition are separate from a private offline runtime inside an encrypted M1 workspace. Hosted agents and external services receive public code, public sources, synthetic fixtures, and aggregate status only.
architecture.data_model: Versioned InputManifest, ReferenceBundle, PhenotypeSet, VariantObservation, CandidateFinding, EvidenceRecord, RunReceipt, and SafeLearning schemas.
architecture.api_contract: No network API. The contract is a versioned CLI plus JSON schemas. Unknown schema versions fail closed.

hermes_integration.boundary: The product owns protected reads, deterministic analysis, scoring, receipts, and reports. Hermes may orchestrate public research and content-free status checks.

risks: Reference mismatch corrupts normalization or annotation.
8 GB memory pressure interrupts a whole-genome prioritization lane.
Single-sample data overstates inheritance or phase.
Missing structural calls are misread as a biological negative.
A generic export path leaks private rows.
A deterministic ranking creates false clinical confidence.
Tool or reference drift silently changes rank.
architecture.privacy: Protected inputs, HPO identifiers, variants, coordinates, genotypes, sample metadata, logs, rankings, and dossier text remain under the encrypted private root. The public projector uses a fixed allowlist and seeded-canary scan.

independent_review.policy: A reviewer who did not implement the change must inspect the exact Git commit and report security, logic, and contract findings

user_journeys: Operator runs the frozen synthetic fixture and receives review_ready with byte-identical artifacts on replay.
Operator runs a private manifest and receives content-free stage status while the detailed dossier stays under the encrypted root.
Operator tampers with a reference receipt and receives stale_receipt before candidate generation.
Operator seeds a protected canary and verifies that the safe projection contains no canary or forbidden private field.

operations.install: Use the project bootstrap for public code. Use the private M1 bootstrap only after the encrypted volume is mounted. Both environments stay separate from Hermes's private environment.
operations.run: Run synthetic acceptance first, then invoke private-run with the trusted manifest inside the encrypted workspace.
operations.health: verify-environment checks mount state, free space, memory, binaries, reference receipts, input receipts, offline policy, and root containment.
operations.rollback: Select the prior verified Git commit, reference bundle receipt, and canonical config. Existing run directories are immutable and never overwritten.
operations.data_backup: The encrypted Expansion workspace and retained FileVault source provide current local custody. Source retirement requires a separate verified recovery and deletion decision.

known_limitations: Research software only. It does not provide diagnosis or treatment advice.
Single-sample data cannot prove inheritance, phase, or de novo status.
The supplied VCF may omit structural or calling classes.
Exomiser and custom evidence rules do not produce calibrated clinical probabilities.
Public sharing and challenge submission remain pending review and approval.
